supersedes.reason: Remove external AgentMux handoff, downstream planning, and adoption-dependent acceptance while preserving the four-task ctxmux Recoverable Stop delivery vertical.

tasks.title: Freeze the complete-session Stop baseline and SSOT
tasks.objective: Independently review the clean b8118aa baseline, make the current Stop and response-loss boundary unambiguous in the owning documentation, and produce one exact committed handoff candidate before changing the protocol.
tasks.outcome: The implementation owner starts Recoverable Stop from a reviewed, clean, fully gated baseline whose docs distinguish strong complete-session cleanup from missing response-loss recovery.
acceptance: The review verifies the current short and attachment Stop shapes, Open-to-Stopping-to-Closed admission, later-mutation fence, direct-child reap and empty-session success proof, graceful/forced receipt, and documented POSIX ownership limits without redesigning them.

The public SSOT states that Stop response loss is currently `unknown`, duplicate ordinary Stop is not receipt recovery, attachment command IDs are connection-local, and `native.recoverable_stop` is not yet advertised.

Vision, architecture, protocol, roadmap, SDK documentation, and Feature Tracker each carry only the facts they own; no second planning document, compatibility promise, Agent semantics, or speculative implementation is introduced.

The documentation checkpoint is committed, the worktree is clean, and `scripts/check.sh` passes on that exact source commit. Verification records the tested commit and tree; later tracker-only lifecycle commits are not presented as a newly tested product candidate.

verification.proves: The reviewed complete-session Stop baseline and documentation checkpoint pass the complete repository contract on one clean source commit.
The independent baseline review, exact tested commit/tree, SSOT disposition, and residual Recoverable Stop gap are auditable.

tasks.title: Ship the Rust recoverable Stop owner vertical
tasks.objective: Add one daemon-instance-bound native Stop operation whose exact terminal result can be joined or recovered after response loss without entering the complete-session Stop owner twice.
tasks.outcome: Rust public clients can retain a Stop operation, reconnect within the same daemon incarnation, recover its exact graceful/forced result, and fail closed on conflicting reuse or daemon replacement.
acceptance: The next protocol generation replaces the pre-stable Stop shape with one explicit operation carrying the original daemon instance, exact Run, and a caller-owned UTF-8 key bounded to 128 bytes; the Runtime advertises `native.recoverable_stop: 1` only when this complete contract is active.

A Runtime-global key index and per-Run admission record permit at most one Stop operation per retained Run. The exact duplicate joins an in-flight attempt or replays its exact settled result; another key for that Run or the same key for another Run returns a typed `not_applied` conflict before mutation.

The existing complete-session Stop state machine remains the only signal, cleanup, reap, and session-quiescence owner. Recoverability wraps its single admission/result and does not add another process walker, signal path, Stop state machine, or general operation framework.

A first response lost after admission remains honestly `unknown` to that call, but retrying the retained exact operation resolves to the original result. Post-admission owner failure is retained or fail-stopped and never permits a second Stop execution under the same or another key.

Deterministic owner tests cover same-key concurrent join, settled replay, different-key and cross-Run conflict, natural exit before admission, response loss, fresh-client retry, daemon replacement, and proof that the Stop owner was entered once.

The repository-owned Recoverable Stop qualification script enumerates and asserts a non-empty Rust owner/client test selection before executing it, so a missing regression cannot produce a green gate.

verification.proves: A non-empty selected set of real native owner and Rust client tests proves one complete-session Stop across concurrent duplicate, response loss, conflicts, replacement, and typed recovery.

tasks.title: Unify attachment, TypeScript, CLI, upgrade, and GC parity
tasks.objective: Expose the same recoverable Stop operation through attachment controls, generated TypeScript, the SDK and CLI, while keeping one bounded daemon ledger continuous across validated planned exec and exact Run collection.
tasks.outcome: Every public local client reaches one daemon-owned Stop result across reconnect and planned exec, and operation retention has one explicit Run-bounded lifecycle.
acceptance: Short requests and attachment Stop controls use the same operation key and daemon ledger. Attachment command IDs remain connection-local correlation; reconnect through either public path with the retained operation returns the same result.

Rust wire types remain the shape SSOT for generated TypeScript declarations, exact runtime validation, SDK exports, and CLI JSON. The low-level Rust and TypeScript APIs require a caller-retainable Stop operation; the CLI supports explicit recovery inputs and may generate a fresh operation only for a one-shot invocation.

The ledger is bounded to at most one admitted entry per retained Run. Run collection removes the Run record and its key index together, prevents collection while settlement still owns mutable state, and permits old-key reuse only after the collection boundary.

A validated planned exec waits for in-flight Stop ownership to settle, carries the complete settled Stop ledger in the versioned handoff manifest, and preserves exact result recovery with the same daemon instance. Cold replacement rejects the old operation and does not claim persisted Stop receipts.

Protocol, architecture decision, SDK and CLI documentation state the capability, result and conflict semantics, first-call `unknown` recovery flow, retention/GC boundary, planned-exec continuity, cold-restart non-goal, and process-session ownership limits.

Real tests cover attachment disconnect, client crash, short-to-attachment and attachment-to-short recovery, planned exec after response loss, collection/key reuse, malformed frames, and TypeScript/CLI parity without weakening existing Stop race and unrelated-process protection tests.
The public parity qualification path asserts a non-empty focused Rust selection and invokes the root SDK E2E entrypoint that builds and injects the real ctxmux binaries.

verification.proves: TypeScript validation, caller-retained operation behavior, conflicts, and wrong cases pass.
The repository root builds the binaries and a public SDK client recovers the exact real-daemon Stop result across disconnect without another Stop.
A non-empty selected owner set proves attachment convergence, planned-exec continuity, bounded collection, and the native process-session oracle together.

tasks.title: Qualify the recoverable Stop contract
tasks.objective: Independently review and qualify the finite recoverable Stop claim on one clean committed ctxmux candidate before advertising it as a public capability.
tasks.outcome: The exact ctxmux commit is a trustworthy public boundary for native Stop recovery, with no open P0/P1 defect and explicit residual limits.
acceptance: One independent read-only review covers operation identity, join/replay algebra, conflict-before-mutation, Stop owner entry count, response-loss and client-crash behavior, attachment convergence, bounded retention, collection, planned exec, daemon replacement, protocol/SDK parity, and process ownership limits.

Every P0/P1 within the accepted claim receives a deterministic regression and re-review. Recoverable Resize/Interrupt, Remote Runtime, crash/host-reboot adoption, AgentSession and Provider semantics, Workbench close transaction, package publication, and external consumer adoption remain outside this Feature.

A clean packed consumer proves Runtime capability discovery, caller-retained Stop preparation, response loss, a fresh client recovering the original graceful/forced receipt, and no second physical Stop effect without repository-private imports.

The complete repository, CI evidence-map, generated-type, documentation-consistency, reliability, and package-consumer gates pass on one exact committed source candidate; verification records that commit and tree.

The Feature closes when that exact qualified ctxmux commit advertises `native.recoverable_stop: 1`, without compatibility shims, migration code, a generic operation framework, a second Stop owner, unfinished scaffolding, or any external consumer plan or code change.

verification.proves: The complete Rust, TypeScript, CLI, reliability, generated-contract, CI-evidence and documentation surface passes together.
An isolated packed consumer recovers one exact Stop result through public artifacts without another Stop effect.
The independent review, exact candidate, capability declaration, finding dispositions, and residual limits are auditable.
